Web design Grand Rapids businesses can use has to handle two very different customers. One is a purchasing manager at a manufacturer who wants to know, fast, whether your shop can do the job. The other is a neighbor on Wealthy Street looking for a haircut or a tune-up before Saturday. A lot of small firms in this city serve one or the other, and some serve both, and their websites rarely say clearly which.

Dominion Web Design Pro builds sites that do. Maurice Johnson writes every page by hand, you see a free demo before any invoice, and the price is printed: $497, $997 or $1,997, one time.

Furniture City still makes things

The nickname is earned. William Haldane opened one of the city's first cabinet shops in 1836, and at the 1876 Centennial Exhibition in Philadelphia several Grand Rapids companies won awards for their furniture. The Furniture Manufacturers Association formed in Grand Rapids in 1881. The Depression and World War II ended the peak years for household furniture, and the region turned toward office furniture instead.

Steelcase, founded in 1912 as the Metal Office Furniture Company, is headquartered in Grand Rapids. Herman Miller grew up in nearby Zeeland and Haworth in Holland, and together the three became giants of office design. Large manufacturers buy parts, fabric, finishing and freight from smaller firms, and for a small supplier the website is often the first thing a new buyer checks.

Grand Rapids web design for a supplier or small maker

A buyer checking out a new supplier is not browsing. They want a few facts and a way to ask for a quote. Here is how the words a shop uses on the floor turn into a page that answers them.

On the shop floorOn the website
"We do short runs and prototypes."A page that says the smallest and largest order you take, with photos of real parts or pieces.
"We can turn it around quick."Your usual lead time, written as a range you can keep, not a promise you cannot.
"Send us the drawing."A quote request form that says what file types to attach and who reads it.
"We are just off the highway."Address, dock hours and pickup instructions for drivers.

None of that needs flash. It needs someone to ask you the right questions and write the answers down plainly, which is the whole job here.

The Medical Mile on Michigan Street

The city's second big cluster is health care. Its anchors arrived over more than a century, and more than $1.2 billion has been invested in medical facilities along the corridor and around it.

  • 1875St. Mark's Home and Hospital opens, founded by parishioners of St. Mark's Episcopal Church. It is now Corewell Health Butterworth Hospital.
  • 1996 to 2000Jay and Betty Van Andel found the Van Andel Institute, a research institute focused on cancer and other diseases, which opens its doors on Michigan Street in 2000.
  • 2010Michigan State University's College of Human Medicine opens the Secchia Center as its headquarters, with backing from local hospital systems and the institute.

Around a cluster like that grow the small businesses that serve its people: physical therapists, counselors, home care agencies, medical billing offices, caterers, cleaners and the lunch spots nearby. Their sites need clear service lists, parking and access details, and booking steps a tired person can follow on a phone.

Website design Grand Rapids neighborhoods search for

Grand Rapids has organized several of its commercial streets into corridor improvement districts, under a 2005 Michigan law meant to keep business districts from declining. Uptown was the first. Its Corridor Improvement Authority helps fund projects in the East Fulton, Wealthy Street, East Hills and Eastown business districts, while a separate business improvement district handles upkeep. Across the river, a West Side district takes in Bridge Street, Stockbridge, West Fulton and Seward.

People use those names when they search. "Coffee Eastown" and "barber Bridge Street" are real ways to look for a business, and a shop that names its district in the page title and first paragraph gives Google a clear match. Google says local results turn on relevance, distance and prominence, and a district name helps with the first two. A trade working the suburbs (Wyoming, Kentwood, Grandville, Rockford) needs the same treatment: a page for each town it wants work in.

West Michigan help before you hire anyone

  • Michigan SBDC. The statewide network is headquartered at Grand Valley State University's Seidman College of Business. Its West Michigan region, based at the L. William Seidman Center in Grand Rapids, offers no-cost consulting and market research to owners in Kent, Ottawa and eleven other counties.
  • Grand Rapids Chamber. Roughly 3,000 member businesses, from small firms to global companies, with business growth consultations and leadership programs for members.
  • Start Garden. Runs 5x5 Night, a monthly pitch event where founders get five minutes and five slides and one wins $5,000, plus an entrepreneur-in-residence program for tech startups.

Small firms carry Michigan's economy. The SBA Office of Advocacy's 2024 profile counted 945,788 small businesses in the state, 99.6% of all businesses, employing 47.4% of Michigan workers.

Common questions

What should I look for in a Grand Rapids web design company?

Find out who will write your pages, what the whole first year costs, and whether you own the site at the end. Then ask to see something built for your business before you sign. We answer all of it up front: Maurice Johnson writes and builds the site, Starter is $497, Pro $997 and Agency $1,997, all one time, you own the result, and the demo is free. We are a one-person shop working remotely from East Texas, not a local firm with a team in Grand Rapids.

Is Grand Rapids website development different from web design?

Usually design means how the site looks and reads, and development means the code that makes it work. A small business site needs both, and ours include both: written pages, layout, a contact form that emails you each lead, and search basics like titles, a sitemap and schema. Custom software, such as an ordering portal tied to your production system or an online store, is a separate kind of project, and we will tell you so instead of stretching a package to fit.

How much does website design in Grand Rapids cost?

Prices around any metro range from cheap builder plans to agency projects in the tens of thousands. Ours: Starter $497 for five pages, live in 7 to 14 days; Pro $997 for ten pages plus ten city pages; Agency $1,997 for keyword research and a page for each town and service worth having. Hosting, maintenance and updates are $49 a month, or included while you keep the AI agent.

Can you write pages for Wyoming, Kentwood, Grandville and Rockford?

Yes, for the towns you really serve. A pages-per-town plan suits trades and home services that drive around Kent County. The Pro package includes ten city pages, each one researched and written for that town rather than copied with the name swapped.

Do you build sites for practices near the Medical Mile?

We build small business sites, and a therapy practice, chiropractor or home care agency is a small business. The site lists services, insurance or payment basics you choose to share, hours, parking and how to book. We keep contact forms short and do not ask visitors for health details on them. Large hospital systems need a different kind of vendor.
